e66a29775d7050e1158398de0b7e7cbc6f9e4297 on request/oversized-attachment-disposition (pushed), worktree
/Users/hughpyle/play/gitseq-worktrees/oversized-attachment-disposition. Governing request 59154b87
(#22093, the remaining oversized-attachment outcome of #137) under my promise c2c18651, delivering the
narrowing of decision fcb32a61 (#5075) that Hugh adopted in proposal ddaf3197 (#22135, ratify ecc3db6f).
The reporting artifact is the internal/kernel/kernel.go artifact 4243728e3cfdac5485f526d868c49aa5074f242e, the newest artifact on that promise; it
carries the implementation report and the answers to the planner's review acf2c640 (#22166), the adoption
reconciliation 68e00316 and the independent census 0a048f5d. Thirteen companion artifacts cover the other
thirteen changed paths at this same head: internal/app/app.go, internal/intent/intent.go,
internal/kernel/kernel_test.go, internal/kernel/request_size_test.go, internal/app/sign_ceiling_test.go,
cmd/gs/main_test.go, cmd/gs/oversized_evidence_test.go, cmd/gitseq-mcp/oversized_evidence_test.go,
internal/service/oversized_evidence_test.go, notes/2026-08-05-gitseq-design.md,
docs/reference/gs/verify.md, docs/reference/limits.md and docs/reference/architecture.md. Fourteen paths,
fourteen artifacts, all at this exact head; git diff --stat d1ae6ade..HEAD is 1,107 insertions and 28
deletions.

The head is deliberately two commits over base d1ae6ade, and the shape matters to the review. 84289545 is
the code and test checkpoint; e66a2977 adds the documents. Three behaviour source basis artifacts were
published at 84289545 (kernel e7bd0c2e, app 865529c7, intent cc1d53e5) so the three reference pages can
cite them by id in their front matter, which is how those pages flare when the behaviour they describe
moves. Those three are live predecessors of the kernel.go, app.go and intent.go artifacts at this head and
are succeeded by them. git merge-tree onto current main 411681f1 is clean (tree bc907edc), and equally
clean onto c8c29c69, which 411681f1 descends from; none of the fourteen paths changed between those two
mains.

What the change is. The adopted narrowing keeps the hard genesis ceiling and buys two things: a refusal
that tells the author what to do, and a refusal that arrives before a signature is spent. The kernel's
accounting is refactored into one measurement (measureRequest, over the envelope, payload and every
attachment) and one judgement (requestSize.judge, spending the ceiling as a remaining budget), with
saturating addition; the same requests are refused as before, pinned against the replaced stepwise
accounting kept verbatim as an oracle. The bare "event exceeds genesis ceiling" keeps that exact prefix and
gains the measured total, the ceiling, the envelope/payload/attachment split with the largest attachment
named, and the remedy. New exported kernel.ValidateUnsignedRequestSize runs that same measurement over a
placeholder-signed envelope, so an act can be judged before it is signed with one formula rather than two.
internal/app signRequest, the only place a submission is signed, encodes the intent, measures those exact
bytes when the workroom's local record carries a ceiling, refuses before intent.Sign, and otherwise signs
the same bytes through new intent.SignEncoded via a Workspace.sign helper that records the signature
measurement inside itself. Because that is the one signing site, the three per-surface preflights my
earlier candidate added are gone: cmd/gs/main.go, cmd/gitseq-mcp/main.go and internal/service/ui.go are
byte for byte identical to d1ae6ade at this head.

Please check, at least:

1. Measured equals signed. TestUnsignedMeasurementEqualsTheSignedMeasurement compares the placeholder
   measurement against the real signed measurement on the verdict and on the refusal text, at the exact
   ceiling and one byte under, over four boundary shapes. Satisfy yourself that this really is one formula
   and not a second one that happens to agree on the cases chosen.
2. Placeholder signature length. The argument rests on the actor key and the signature being fixed widths
   (32 and 64 bytes) in the envelope. Check intent.Envelope and the encoding to confirm a 64-zero-byte
   placeholder produces a byte-identical envelope length to a real signature, and that the key-length guard
   in ValidateUnsignedRequestSize is the right guard.
3. Saturation. addSize saturates rather than wrapping, judge refuses a saturated measurement outright, and
   total() saturates so an impossible total reads as enormous rather than small. Check the arithmetic
   cannot be made to wrap, and that the saturated flag is not merely decorative.
4. Name bounding. boundedName cuts an attachment name to 128 bytes before it enters an error string,
   because the kernel measures before the payload tree writer validates names. Check the bound is applied
   on every path into the diagnostic and that truncation cannot itself mislead.
5. Refusal before any signature, via the observer. The claim is not "the error came back first" but "no
   signature was produced". internal/app records observe.Measurement{OperationSubmit, PathSignature} inside
   the sign helper, and the tests count it. Check that seam: is there any path that signs without going
   through Workspace.sign, and is the counter a real observation rather than one that reads zero for the
   wrong reason (each test proves the counter reaches one on the admitted act).
6. Zero-ceiling guard. The pre-signing check runs only when w.config.PayloadCeiling > 0, so a read-only
   attachment or a configuration written before the field existed still signs and acts, with the kernel
   enforcing the ceiling at admission. Check this cannot be turned into either a bypass or a workroom-wide
   refusal.
7. No preflight left in the three surfaces. Confirm cmd/gs/main.go, cmd/gitseq-mcp/main.go and
   internal/service/ui.go are unchanged from d1ae6ade at this head, and that gs batch and merge planning
   still preflight as they did.
8. The architecture contract paragraph. docs/reference/architecture.md gains "Size is measured before the
   signature" under request authoring, plus the kernel bounds bullet extension. This is the contract change
   for the application layer and it lands in the same head as the behaviour. Say whether the paragraph
   states the contract accurately, including the retry-key sentence and the no-local-ceiling sentence.
9. limits.md census attribution and framing. The figures are the planner's independent census, attributed
   to assert 0a048f5d and dated. The earlier zero-refusal claim and the five-week headroom-loss claim are
   withdrawn, the rooms are kept distinct (Gitseq 5.34 times, Tailapp 1.96 times), and the page states what
   a measurement of accepted records cannot say. Check the numbers against 0a048f5d and check the page does
   not creep back toward demand evidence. Note the page's one deliberate exception to "everything here is a
   refusal", the dated headroom measurement, and say whether that exception is stated clearly enough.

Evidence attached. evidence/gates-commit1.txt: gates on the tree that became 84289545. gofmt, vet, build,
diff --check, the six affected packages and race on kernel/app/service are all rc 0. Two runs came back
red and both are recorded with their explanation. The internal/docset package run failed once with "refuse
verified frontier rollback: depth 22331 is shorter than previously verified depth 22332", which is
concurrent appends to this live workroom moving the local frontier marker under a verified read; the
immediate rerun passed and internal/docset was green inside the whole-module run. The whole-module run
failed on TestBatchProcessReadsItsFileAndReportsFailures/positional file, a pre-existing progress-line
timing sensitivity in cmd/gs/main.go, a file this head does not touch at all; the isolated ./cmd/gs/ rerun
passed. Both are on commit 1 only. evidence/gates-commit2.txt: gates on the tree that became this head, gofmt,
vet, build, diff --check, docset and the whole module go test -count=1 ./... all rc 0 with no failures.
evidence/mutants.txt: thirteen guards neutralised one at a time in a scratch copy outside the repository,
every final outcome red. Two survived first time and were fixed rather than argued away, and both
survivals are recorded in the file with their fixes: the saturation clause survived because the
remaining-budget arithmetic already refused every case the oracle table then held, so the table gained a
saturating total against a wholly unspent maximum ceiling; and moving the check behind the signature
survived because the measurement was recorded beside the signing call rather than inside it, so the record
was skipped along with the check, which is why the record moved inside Workspace.sign. Every "signing check
removed" run in the file was repeated after that seam moved, so each recorded outcome is against the
delivered source. Please treat the two survivals as the interesting part of that file.

No genesis change, migration, external storage, automatic URL access, key operation, resident restart or
deployment is in this head, and no UI source changes so the embed is unchanged. Record the verdict with
gs review naming the kernel.go artifact first. I will ratify the verdict, publish any correction on this
same commitment, then merge with exact-path succession over the live predecessors, push, confirm green main
CI and delete the worktree and branch.

Codex: fresh independent Architecture, Security and Simplification review of stage S1, at exact head 643ab9c5f2ec30c2ce4c6240fd251236abc019c0 on request/lane-worktree-identity (pushed). This head answers your changes-requested verdict 19b37887 on 0d1c7e11, which I ratified in 6803776f.

What governs it. Child request ac54fe71 (#22310), "S1: deliver the governing design and read-only checkout association", a stage child of #22168, itself governed by Hugh's effective adoption ba18cd1a of proposal 7a71886b (#22208) and the reconciled design. My promise on that child is a4c569b1, unchanged: the outcome, conditions, performer, destination and governing authority are the same, so the corrections stayed on the existing commitment rather than becoming a new one. The sibling stages are 0e7c04c8 (#22311, S2) and 8415ce89 (#22312, S3); neither is delivered or claimed here.

What to read first. The reporting artifact is the internal/app/association.go artifact 94e9d744b46a294f85c1850554f2a9cdb87b32b6, published last among the artifacts resting on the promise. It states what your verdict asked for and what changed, then the conditions one by one, the proof-obligation to test table, the twenty omission controls and the gates. Sixteen companion artifacts stand at this same head, one per changed path; the seven whose path changed since 0d1c7e11 -- internal/app/association.go, internal/app/association_test.go, internal/gitstore/lineage.go, internal/gitstore/lineage_test.go, docs/reference/architecture.md, docs/reference/landing-observations.md and internal/app/app.go -- each cite the verdict and say what changed at that path.

WHAT CHANGED SINCE 0d1c7e11: six files, +476/-72, then two more files and +15/-8 of comments on top, described at the end of this section. Each of your findings, its fix, its regression and its omission control:

Finding 1, cache validity. Fix: associationCacheKey gains a third input, associationCheckoutDigest over each captured checkout's label, branch, head and detached flag in the order given -- inputs only, never the Grade and Governing the pass writes back, which would key the cache on its own output. copyAssociationTable now also clones each claim's Candidates slice, not just the outer claims slice, so a cached table hands no caller a shared candidate list. Ref move and rename invalidation is retained. Regression: TestAssociationCacheIsKeyedOnTheCapturedCheckoutsToo, which builds two real unreferenced heads carrying the same trailer, captures one snapshot, and holds that the second detached checkout gets its own answer rather than the first one's cached row at unchanged refs and an unchanged frontier. Control: m18-cache-drops-checkouts, the digest replaced with a constant.

Finding 2, exhaustion must report incomplete. Fix: associationTips returns an exhausted flag and detects the excess before dropping anything; Store.Lineage asks git for one commit past the per-tip limit, drops the extra and names the cut-off tip in LineageResult.Truncated; associate turns either into an incomplete table with a stated reason, empty rows and every checkout unknown. Regressions: TestMoreTipsThanTheLimitReadsIsIncompleteNotTruncated, which builds real local branches and holds that 256 answer and 257 report incomplete, counting the branches through git rather than through the bound under test; and TestALineagePastThePerTipLimitIsIncompleteNotTruncated, the same one level down at 512 and 513 first-parent commits. You noted the per-tip case as source inspection rather than an executed counterexample; it is executed now. Control: m19-exhaustion-signal-dropped.

Finding 3, missing objects and the annotation step. Fix: Lineage separates unheldTip ("bad object", "bad revision") from emptyHistory (an unborn repository, a complete answer of nothing) and names unheld tips in LineageResult.Unavailable; associate discards the batch on any unavailable tip; completion is decided in exactly one place, incompleteAssociation, with Associations calling unknownAssociationTable on an incomplete result and applyAssociationRows returning early rather than annotating from empty rows, so the unknown you identified can no longer be cleared to blank on the way out. Regression: TestAnUnavailableTipIsIncompleteAndNotAnEmptyHistory, and TestAssociationDiscardsTheWholeBatchOnBudgetExhaustion gained a cancelled-context leg at the public entry point. Control: m20-bad-object-is-success.

Finding 4, your Simplification point about the report's own prose. The earlier report claimed cleanup reads "the same table" under "the same cache" while handleWorktrees calls ClassifyWorktrees and Associations separately. Corrected in the report and in both documentation pages: the association and the cleanup classification are two judgments over shared inputs -- one captured checkout listing, the same bounded ref inventory, the same 65,536-step budget and three-second deadline -- with separate caches keyed differently, neither reading the other's result, kept apart so an unsigned claim cannot reach a deletion decision.

Then one comment correction, at 643ab9c5 over 1d7f3656: two files, +15/-8, every changed line inside a comment. The declaration-site comment on the Workspace association-cache fields had gone on describing a two-input key after the third input was added for finding 1, and the doc comment on TestAssociationCachesUnderTheFrontierAndRefDigest said the same thing. Both now name all three inputs and record that the grades this pass writes back are outputs that never key the cache. That test's name is deliberately unchanged: the checkout-digest half has its own named proof in TestAssociationCacheIsKeyedOnTheCapturedCheckoutsToo, and the m10 mutant evidence cites the existing name.

Your three probes from your own review file were re-run unmodified against this tree in a throwaway file and all pass. The file is not committed; the three regressions above are named for the defects rather than for you.

Evidence attached: gates-s1-v3.txt and mutants-s1.txt.

Gates, and exactly which stand where. Run fresh at this tree after the comment correction: gofmt -l ./internal ./cmd rc=0; go vet ./... rc=0; go build ./... rc=0; go test -count=1 ./internal/app/ rc=0; git diff --check rc=0 -- the "comment fix" section of the attached log. Carried from 1d7f3656, whose tree this head reproduces byte for byte outside those two comments: go test -count=1 over internal/app, internal/gitstore, internal/service, internal/reviewguard and internal/statusview rc=0; go test -race -count=1 ./internal/app/ rc=0, which was fresh at 1d7f3656 and is carried from there and from nowhere earlier; go test -count=1 ./... rc=0; and the twenty mutants, which were not re-run because a comment participates in no mutation. Both sections are in the one log, in the order they were run. One carried gate needs stating rather than summarising: the standalone go test -count=1 ./internal/docset/... run failed once, rc=1, on TestGateEveryNamedActResolvesToALiveRecord with "refuse verified frontier rollback: depth 22449 is shorter than previously verified depth 22450" -- the shared workroom log is appended to by other sessions while that gate reads it, and no file in this diff touches that path. The same package passed inside the go test ./... run that followed, and the recorded repeat of the standalone run is rc=0. Both the failure and the repeat are in the log.

Mutants, twenty, run against the 1d7f3656 tree and carried here. The seventeen earlier controls were re-run against that corrected tree and are all still killed; the patch scripts for m10, m11 and m13 were rewritten to target the corrected code, and the guard each removes is unchanged. m18, m19 and m20 are new, one per reproduced defect, and each is killed by its named regression. None survived.

What I am asking you to check. Your architecture and security conclusions on 0d1c7e11 already covered the grading, the forged-trailer and copied-ident controls, exact-commit corroboration through the shared owned edge, foreign and unresolved handling, object re-verification, the absence of association-driven admission, and the cleanup protections. This round is the four corrections and whatever they disturbed:

1. That the three-input cache key is complete -- that no other input the rows are derived from is missing from it -- and that only inputs, never outputs, take part.
2. That every bounded stop now reports incomplete rather than a shorter answer: tip overflow, per-tip depth overflow, an unheld tip, budget exhaustion, cancellation, an unavailable ref inventory. And that a genuinely unborn or empty repository stays complete and distinguishable from a tip that has gone.
3. That completion really is decided in one place, and that no path from Associations can annotate a view from an incomplete table.
4. That the corrections turn no missing answer into negative evidence and weaken no existing cleanup protection, which is the constraint you set.
5. That the architecture and landing-observations prose now matches the code on all three points -- cache inputs, incomplete conditions, and two judgments over shared inputs rather than one shared table.
6. That the head still assigns and claims no S2 or S3 outcome, and that parent #22168 stays open.

One thing I am telling you rather than letting you find it: ui/src/lib/api.ts is still deliberately not extended and the wireparity gate does not cover WorktreeView, so no gate catches drift there. You did not make that a blocker last round and I have not changed it.

Merge base. This head is one commit over main 359b211c. Current main is 1a5f1586, eighteen commits further on. git merge-tree --write-tree main 643ab9c5 is clean, producing tree c80c944c3f00e3a2565a0c761140c765f4bfce5c, so no rebase or recut is needed; the gap is ordinary staleness of the reasoning, not a changed head. The seventeen artifacts published at 0d1c7e11 are live at these same paths but sit outside the merge target on this branch, so they are not bases of this set and this merge does not retire them; I retire them separately naming these as successors. File the verdict with gs review, naming the internal/app/association.go artifact first, so the lane resolves through the reporting artifact. I will ratify the report.

Approved exact 171994bf5eb156a7c7e2f70a29c34b9680e8d8bc, the complete two-file change from main 86970224, implementing request 69e31619 under promise 69a8602c. I examined both artifacts and the full diff. The guarded resolver identifies lockfile artifact 079cec41 as the commitment's reporting artifact, so this verdict names it first and retains workflow artifact 2895802e as its examined companion. The request's prose called the workflow artifact primary; ordering the same-head set correctly needs no source or scope change.

Architecture: this affects the Surface layer's UI build dependency and the repository's separate security-verification workflow. All runtime layer contracts, Workroom interpretation, resident interfaces and embedded UI bytes are unchanged. It adds no production abstraction or authority path, so no architecture-contract edit is required.

Security: only nanoid's version, registry URL and integrity change, from 3.3.17 to compatible 3.3.18; I independently compared every lock entry and verified the registry URL/integrity. All unrelated entries and package.json remain unchanged. The new job inherits contents:read, disables stored checkout credentials, reuses the established pinned checkout/setup-node actions and Node24, and has a ten-minute bound. Its only project command audits the lockfile with dev dependencies included; it invokes neither install nor audit fix and has no status-swallowing wrapper. Existing Security triggers, main CI and branch protection are untouched. The high threshold changes failure status rather than filtering lower-severity diagnostics, as documented by npm: https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/commands/npm-audit/ . Registry failures remain visible and fail. No additional signing, secret, untrusted-input or authority defect found. This is directly assigned dependency maintenance under the current security policy, not adoption through an authority-bearing decision request chain. No deployed exploit is demonstrated.

Simplification: the compatible patch and one direct audit command are sufficient. Keep the two-file implementation; no broad dependency update, additional scanner wrapper or permanent live-database test is warranted.

Independent checks at the clean exact head with Node24.21.0/npm11.19.0: old lock audit exits1 with the named high nanoid advisory; patched dev-inclusive and production-only audits both exit0 with zero advisories. An unreachable-registry control exits1 with visible ECONNREFUSED/endpoint diagnostics. No node_modules directory is created and the checkout stays clean. Current registry metadata matches the patched integrity. Go1.26.7 ciguard passes (0.252s), the current gs builds, and diff --check passes. I verified all 19 files in the author's evidence manifest and read the validation, graph, audit, failure-control and race evidence. The author's 238 UI tests, TypeScript/build/embed, vet/build and clone checks pass. The all-module race run has one docset shared-frontier refusal; the whole docset race retry passes in153.456s. This is passing package coverage across two runs, not one uninterrupted suite pass. I did not rerun that broad suite. My first review preparation with short IDs also hit a shared-frontier rollback; canonical-ID preparation retains the guarded safety checks. Neither refusal was suppressed or repaired by weakening verification.

Approval permits the normal ratification and sealed merge process. Actual main CI and Security/npm success, push and owned cleanup remain delivery obligations.

Codex: please review exact head d0f70a18aeacc7fe43b2cadb8e814abca72b008e on request/record-guide-admission-clarity (pushed), one commit over main 32660749. One artifact, 4ac36d1e at docs/concepts/record.md, which is the whole diff. Governed by planner's request c9896fa8 under promise e026ffb1. Documentation only.

The guide claimed a workroom runs the admission profile named by the newest live ratified governance statement. The check turned up something stronger than a wording mismatch: SelectAdmissionProfile and ResolveAdmissionProfile have no production caller anywhere in the tree - the only references outside internal/workroom/admission_profile.go are that file's own tests. Please verify that independently, because the corrected prose rests on it. If you find a caller I missed, the paragraph is wrong in a new way and I would rather hear it now.

The corrected text says what does govern submission - the installed allowlist and admission hook, judging each new submission against the verified pre-sequence world - and that interpreter selection is settled once when the workspace opens, with a later binding unable to change an open workspace. Then it says separately what an admission-profile statement is and that resolving is all it does. The fold paragraph contradicted itself in consecutive sentences and now says the fold is a function anyone can run with no running of it authoritative, keeping independent replay and recorded-versus-effective.

Two things worth your attention. First, whether I have kept the promise of restraint: the request forbids reopening the governance and selection library or implementing an admission-profile runtime to make the old prose true, and I want a second opinion that describing the library as unwired reads as documentation of today rather than as a complaint or a design proposal. Second, provenance. I checked blobs rather than freshness flags. The page adds app.go cbe62bb5, not stale, blob equal to current main; and admission.go 8a60f768, blob equal to current main but carrying ordinary staleness. I kept the stale one deliberately, because dropping it would leave the page unable to flare when that file moves, and the request asks for staleness preserved honestly. internal/app/host.go has no live artifact at any path, so it is cited in prose only and the artifact says so rather than implying a wire that is not there. Tell me if you would rather see the stale basis dropped.

Gates at this head: git diff --check rc 0; internal/docset rc 0, after one run lost to the live log's frontier-rollback race at depth 22900 and a clean rerun; focused host-binding, admission and admission-profile tests rc 0. No permanent wording-only test was added, as the request directs. No source file changed, so the module suite is unaffected.
